memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: When Moses sent them to explore Canaan, he said, "Go up through the Negev and on into the hill country. See what the land is like and whether the people who live there are strong or weak, few or many. What kind of land do they live in? Is it good or bad? What kind of towns do they live in? Are they unwalled or fortified? How is the soil? Is it fertile or poor? Are there trees in it or not? Do your best to bring back some of the fruit of the land." (It was the season for the first ripe grapes.) — Num 13:17-20 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses gives careful, practical instructions. He wants real information — about the people, the towns, the soil, the fruit. There is nothing unspiritual about gathering facts. Faith is not the same as burying your head in the sand and pretending obstacles do not exist. God expects us to look clearly at reality.

This is worth remembering, because sometimes we imagine that trusting God means ignoring the hard facts. But Moses sends the men to observe everything honestly — the strong people, the fortified cities, the quality of the land. The information itself was not the problem. The problem, as we will see, was how the men interpreted what they saw.

The same facts can be read two ways. Ten spies would look at the strong people and fortified towns and conclude, "We cannot do this." Two would look at the very same things and conclude, "With God, we can." The difference was not the data but the faith through which the data was viewed.

So it is with us. Faith does not deny reality; it sees reality in the light of God. Yes, the diagnosis is serious. Yes, the bills are real. Yes, the situation is genuinely hard. Faith looks all of it full in the face — and then looks higher still, to the God who is greater than every fortified wall. Bring back the fruit; face the facts; but never forget who goes before you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you tend to ignore hard facts, or face them honestly before God?
2. How can two people look at the same situation and respond so differently?
3. What "fortified walls" are you facing that God is bigger than?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, help me to face reality honestly without fear. Give me eyes of faith that see my circumstances in the light of Your greatness. Let me never forget that You are bigger than every obstacle. Amen.
